summary: Willamette NF lookout site: tent station c.1914, cab built c.1930 (sources give 1928, 1930 or 1931), abandoned and burned in 1968; registers say it is now gone.

facts.design: D-6 cab; a 1967 memo calls it a standard-type lookout of 196 square feet
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1968 and disposed of by burning; the register says it is now gone

visit.trail_note: Frissell Trail #3512 climbs from the Frissell South Trailhead to Frissell Ridge, with views over the McKenzie River Valley

events.note: Established as a tent camp with an alidade for locating fires (register: about 1914)
1919 season: Dorothy Andrews, twin of Martha, at Frissell Point, per a July 1920 Sunday Oregonian item
Dorothy Dickey named in a June 1920 Oregon Daily Journal item as the coming season's lookout
Walter Sackman reported at the lookout in September 1920
Ethel Neal (also printed Neil) at the station; a cougar near her cabin was reported in August 1921
Wallace Halsey described as forest ranger at the lookout station
Register: D-6 cab erected 1930; a July-August 1930 newspaper item describes construction; firelookout.com gives 1928 and a 1967 memo gives 1931
Horace Smith described as fire lookout
Forest Service memo: not manned for a couple of years; disposal proposed and agreed by fire control
Disposed of by burning, per the lookout history

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1928 (firelookout.com), 1930 (register; 1930 newspaper items describe construction) and 1931 (1967 memo). The story reports the disagreement rather than choosing one.
The 1920s newspapers name the Cascade National Forest; the register uses the Willamette National Forest. The story uses the current name.

A June 1920 Oregon Daily Journal item names Dorothy Dickey for the coming season; a July 1920 Sunday Oregonian item names Dorothy Andrews for the 1919 season. The sources do not say whether they are the same woman, so the story does not link them.

firelookout.com gives about four miles northeast; the 1920-1931 newspaper items give 15, seven, seven and eight miles. The story gives the four-mile figure with its source and reports the newspaper range.

notes_for_editor: Newspaper items are read from the Rex's Fire Lookout Page transcriptions, not the original papers, which were not checked. Spellings vary (Frissell, Frissel, Frisell, Frizelle). Both registers say the site is gone. Access level is not set: no source says whether the site is open. The last manned year is not stated; the 1967 memo implies the station had been empty for a couple of years. No photo URLs with credits were found. The Frissell Point Facebook video result was not used as a source.
